parsed.why: Most-protective tier: public accommodations, hate-crime coverage, shield law shielding visiting patients, mandated gender-neutral toilets, X markers. National border, facility and custody rules still bind the visitor, capping below reduced risk.

Public accommodations and hate-crime coverage with demonstrated enforcement (2026 civil-rights conviction), but no local shield, surgery-only birth certificates, and a high raw incident count plus 'least safe in region' label lacking a denominator.

Statewide March 2025 sex-definition statute covers bathrooms, lockers, shelters, dorms and prisons — tier-1 universal exposure; no statewide nondiscrimination, plus a religious-refusal statute licensing service denial. Adds a hostile layer over the national regime.

Nondiscrimination since 2001 including accommodations and healthcare, hate-crime enhancements, X markers, shield laws, panic defence repealed. No enforcement data documented, single-occupancy toilets only, and national border, facility and custody rules remain universal exposures.

Facility ban reaches only school students, so no adult universal exposure; but no statewide nondiscrimination, hate-crime statute excludes gender identity, and an RFRA-style statute enables service refusal — thin recourse over the shared hostile national framework.
